summary:
Build a spacecraft. Walk inside it. Send one last signal home.

NOVA SHIFT is a space mission game that you play in your web browser. You design your own lunar-orbit spacecraft. Then you step inside and walk through it in first person.

Your mission is simple, but it is not easy:

Bring the generator online, Run the science instruments, Send a signal to Earth.

The ship talks to you. Lights, screens and alarms show you how healthy it is. Outside the windows, you can see the Moon, Earth and Sun.

You make the design choices. You keep the systems running. You finish each task in the right order. This is how real space missions work.
details:
PROJECT OVERVIEW:

NOVA SHIFT: The Last Signal is a single-player 3D space mission game that runs in a web browser. Players design a spacecraft for a lunar-orbit mission, then step inside it in first person to restore power, operate science equipment, maintain communications with Earth, and complete mission objectives before time runs out.

The project turns the behind-the-scenes work of a space mission into an experience people can try for themselves. The Moon, Earth, and Sun are visible outside the spacecraft, while screens, lights, sounds, and alarms show the condition of the ship’s systems. The game is designed for computers and phones, and does not require an app installation.

WHAT DOES THE PROJECT DO, AND HOW DOES IT WORK?

The game connects spacecraft design with mission operations. In the Shipyard, players choose spacecraft parts while considering the mission’s budget, mass, power, communications, and science requirements. Once the design is validated and launched, the player explores the ship in first person and uses its consoles to manage the mission.

The main mission begins with the spacecraft’s power offline. Players must restart the generator, route power to essential systems, repair and align the antenna, operate science instruments, collect data, and transmit it to Earth. Events such as solar flares, power surges, and antenna failures create additional challenges. Mission objectives and a ten-minute timer help players track their progress.

The project includes three mission profiles:

•⁠ ⁠Lunar Echo: Analyze a lunar signal and transmit the results to Earth.

•⁠ ⁠Lunar Survey: Collect geological and seismic data.

•⁠ ⁠Deep Space Relay: Establish a communications link and send test data.

HOW DOES IT ADDRESS THE CHALLENGE?

Space missions depend on careful planning, systems management, and problem-solving, but most people do not get to see this work up close. NOVA SHIFT makes some of those responsibilities visible and interactive. Players make design decisions, manage competing needs, respond to equipment problems, and see how one system can affect the rest of the mission.

The game presents these ideas through exploration and play instead of relying only on explanations. Players can see the equipment, visit the rooms where it is used, and observe how the ship responds to their actions.

WHY IS THIS IMPORTANT?

Space exploration can feel distant or difficult to understand. NOVA SHIFT offers an accessible way to explore the teamwork and engineering concepts behind a mission. It can help introduce players to ideas such as power management, communications, payload planning, scientific data collection, and troubleshooting.

The project is intended to spark curiosity about space and engineering, particularly among students and people who may not have encountered mission operations before. Its educational impact is an intended outcome; the project materials do not include formal learning evaluations.

WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

NOVA SHIFT gives players an active role in a space mission. They can explore a spacecraft, make design choices, operate systems, and respond to changing conditions.

The game also connects engineering tradeoffs to mission outcomes. Players must consider factors such as mass, cost, power, battery capacity, communications range, and science requirements. This can encourage systems thinking and show why missions depend on planning as well as technical equipment.

Because it runs in a browser and supports both desktop and touch controls, players can access it without installing a dedicated application.

WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT?

The intended impact is to make space mission work more understandable and engaging. By giving players a chance to manage a spacecraft and complete a mission, NOVA SHIFT aims to encourage interest in space exploration, engineering, and problem-solving.

Players should come away with a stronger sense that a mission depends on connected systems, careful preparation, and calm responses when something goes wrong.

WHAT TOOLS DID THE TEAM USE?

The project was built with React and TypeScript, with Vite for development and production builds. Three.js, through React Three Fiber and related libraries, provides the 3D graphics. Zustand manages the game and interface state.

The project uses the Web Audio API to generate music, ambient sound, and sound effects in code. A small Node.js server serves the built game, and the site is hosted on Render. The team also used Claude, an AI assistant, during development.

HOW IS THE PROJECT CREATIVE?

NOVA SHIFT combines a spacecraft design experience with a first-person mission inside the spacecraft. The ship that players assemble in the Shipyard becomes the ship they operate during the mission.

The project also creates much of its visual and audio content procedurally. Space scenery, spacecraft parts, textures, and sound are generated by code, so the game does not depend on external image or audio files. The spacecraft’s screens, lighting, alarms, and room-specific sounds help communicate the state of its systems as part of the environment.

WHAT FACTORS DID THE TEAM CONSIDER?

The project reflects several design considerations:

•⁠ ⁠Approachability: A guided tutorial, clear objectives, validation messages, and prompts help players learn the controls and mission systems.

•⁠ ⁠Interconnected systems: The spacecraft design affects how much power, battery capacity, communications capability, and science equipment are available during the mission.

•⁠ ⁠Device access: Desktop players use keyboard and mouse controls, while phones and tablets have touch controls for movement, looking around, and interacting.

•⁠ ⁠Performance: Graphics settings allow players to reduce visual detail on slower devices, and phones start with lower graphics settings.

•⁠ ⁠Feedback: Screens, lights, sounds, and alarms communicate changes in the spacecraft’s condition.

•⁠ ⁠Resource constraints: The game’s procedural visuals and audio reduce reliance on separate media assets.

SCOPE AND CONSIDERATIONS

NOVA SHIFT is a single-player game with a simplified mission simulation. It is designed to make mission operations engaging and understandable, rather than to serve as a complete spacecraft engineering or flight simulation tool.

Project documentation states that settings, tutorial completion, and saved spacecraft designs are stored in the browser. It also states that the game does not send gameplay data over the network and that the server does not store player data.
